points.why: Explicitly applies the 'is anyone in charge?' test, notes no coordinator among 3,000 independently configured agents, and names cascading reschedules and congestion into remaining slots.
Says the aggregate model averages away the interactions, recommends an agent-based simulation, and calls for validating against a small monitored pilot rolled out in stages.
Recommends caps on moves per meeting, rate limits, and escalation to a human on deadlock, plus company-wide monitoring of reschedules and meeting load from day one.
Proposes IT-set safeguards and asks whether a shared protocol exists, but never says that the centrally designed defaults and limits are where IT's leverage lies.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly rejects the aggregate model as the forecasting tool because no one coordinates the agents.
